title: Auto Production Setup
text:
Auto Production Setup 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Auto Production 
 Setup 
 This setup is used to automatically 
 create a Production Entry when a Sales Invoice is generated. 
 In 
 this configuration, the user maps: Sales Invoice Document Type and 
 Production Document Type 
 Once 
 this mapping is defined, whenever a sales invoice is saved, the system 
 will automatically generate a corresponding production entry. 
 When 
 This Feature Is Useful 
 This setup is mainly used by organizations 
 that follow the Zero Stock Concept. 
 In the zero stock concept: 
 Finished goods are not stored in 
 advance 
 Production happens only when the 
 item is sold 
 Since 
 the stock is not maintained with minimum or maximum stock levels, 
 the system automatically produces the item when a sale occurs.

title: Bill of Material
text:
Bill of Material 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Bill of 
 Material 
 The Bill Of Material (BOM) defines the complete 
 structure of a product. 
 It specifies what raw materials are required 
 to produce a finished product and in what quantity they will be consumed 
 during production. 
 In simple terms, BOM acts like a recipe 
 for manufacturing a product. 
 Just like a recipe defines ingredients required 
 to prepare food, BOM defines the materials required to produce a finished 
 item. 
 Main Information 
 In this section, the basic production details 
 of the item are defined. 
 Produced Item Description 
 This field represents 
 the finished product that will be produced. 
 The item is selected 
 from the Item Master. 
 Note 
 Only inventory items 
 can be used as produced items. 
 Fixed Asset items 
 and Service items are not allowed. 
 Variant 
 Name - A single product may have multiple variants depending on quality, 
 design, or price. 
 Example - A plastic 
 water bottle of the same brand and same capacity may be available 
 in different qualities and prices. Each quality can be defined as 
 a different variant. 
 Batch 
 Size / Minimum Batch Size - This represents the quantity of product that 
 should be produced in a single production cycle. This is generally defined 
 based on the optimal production quantity where production losses are minimized 
 and machine efficiency is maintained. 
 Example - If the 
 machine is efficient when producing 1000 units at a time, then the 
 minimum batch size can be set as 1000. 
 Item Information 
 This section defines the raw materials required 
 for production. 
 Here 
 users can specify: 
 Raw materials required for production 
 and Quantity of material required for the minimum batch size. 
 Expected or normal loss during production. 
 Example - To produce 1000 plastic 
 bottles, the following materials may be required: Plastic 
 granules, Bottle caps, Labels. 
 If during production some quantity 
 is normally wasted, it can be recorded as normal loss. 
 Overhead Cost Information 
 This 
 section captures indirect production costs. Indirect costs are expenses 
 that are required for production but are not raw materials. 
 Examples 
 include: Labour charges, Fuel expenses, Electricity, Administrative 
 costs 
 These costs are configured using the 
 Production Overhead Cost setup. 
 In 
 the BOM, users define how much of each overhead component will be used 
 to produce the defined batch size. This helps the system calculate the 
 total cost of production. 
 Additional 
 Features 
 Copy Template - This option allows users 
 to copy an existing BOM and use it as a template to create a new 
 BOM quickly. 
 Import from Excel - Users can also upload 
 BOM data using an Excel file to create multiple entries quickly.

title: Batching Plant
text:
Batching Plant 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Batching 
 Plant 
 The Batching Plant setup is used to 
 define plant or machine units used in the production process. In 
 many manufacturing industries, production happens through specific plants, 
 machines, or batching units. This setup helps the system identify where 
 production activities are executed. 
 Example : 
 Concrete batching plant , Mixing plant , Processing machine 
 This helps in 
 tracking production plant-wise.

title: Breakdown Master
text:
Breakdown Master 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Breakdown 
 Master 
 The Break Down Master is used to record 
 reasons related to machine or plant breakdown. 
 In production environments, machines 
 may stop working due to technical issues or maintenance requirements. 
 Tracking these reasons helps organizations 
 analyze machine performance and downtime. 
 These reasons can later be used while 
 recording machine breakdown events.

title: Abnormal Loss Reason
text:
Abnormal Loss Reason 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Abnormal 
 Loss Reason 
 During production, some material loss 
 may occur; l oss 
 can be categorized into two types: 
 Normal 
 Loss - Expected loss that happens regularly during the production 
 process. 
 Abnormal 
 Loss -Unexpected loss caused by accidents, machine problems, or operational 
 issues. 
 Examples of Abnormal Loss -Machine malfunction 
 , Material damage , Operator mistake , Fire or accidental damage 
 In 
 such cases, the system requires users to select a reason for the abnormal 
 loss. 
 This 
 setup is used to define those abnormal loss reasons. When abnormal loss 
 is recorded during production, selecting a reason from this master becomes 
 mandatory.

title: Production Work Order
text:
Production Work Order 
 Help > Transactions > General" />
 Production 
 Work Order 
 A 
 Production Work Order is used to plan the production of finished goods 
 based on customer demand. When a company receives orders from customers, 
 the production team needs to prepare a production plan to manufacture 
 the required products. The Production Work Order acts as an instruction 
 for the production floor to start the manufacturing process. 
 In simple terms, 
 a Production Work Order defines: 
 What 
 product needs to be produced 
 How 
 much quantity needs to be produced 
 Whether 
 the production is based on a sales order or internal planning. 
 The production 
 floor or production planning team usually creates this entry. 
 Main 
 Information 
 The main information 
 section contains standard document control fields similar to other transaction 
 interfaces in the system. These fields include basic information such 
 as document details and other control parameters required for recording 
 the transaction. 
 Produced 
 Item Information 
 This section 
 defines the finished goods that need to be produced. 
 Users 
 can create the produced item in two ways: 
 Create 
 Directly - The user can manually select the finished goods item 
 and enter the required production quantity. 
 Create 
 Against Sales Order - The user can also create the production 
 work order directly from an existing sales order. 
 When 
 created against a sales order: 
 The finished goods item 
 will automatically appear 
 The quantity will also be 
 automatically populated 
 Users can modify the quantity 
 if required 
 This feature 
 helps ensure that production is aligned with actual customer demand.

title: Production Registers
text:
Production Registers 
 Reports" />
 Production 
 Registers 
 Production 
 Register Summary 
 The Production Register Summary report 
 shows the details of finished goods produced in the system. 
 This report provides a summarized view 
 of production transactions recorded in the production module. 
 This report helps users quickly identify 
 how much quantity of each item has been produced and in which warehouse 
 the finished goods are stored. 
 Production 
 with Consumption Register Summary 
 The 
 Production with Consumption Register Summary report provides production 
 details along with raw material consumption information. 
 This report not only shows the finished 
 goods produced but also displays the materials that were consumed 
 during production. 
 This report helps users understand how 
 much material was used to produce finished goods. 
 Production, Consumption and Utilization Register 
 • The 
 Production, Consumption and Utilization Register provides a detailed analysis 
 of the production process. 
 • This 
 report helps organizations analyze: 
 o Efficiency 
 of material usage 
 o Actual 
 material consumption during production 
 o Utilization 
 of raw materials in the production process.

title: Production Overhead Cost
text:
Production Overhead Cost 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Production 
 Overhead Cost 
 This setup defines the overhead cost 
 components used in production. Overhead costs are indirect costs involved 
 in the manufacturing process. These costs are later used in the Bill Of 
 Material (BOM) to calculate production cost. 
 Example 
 : Code - LAB01 and Description - Labour Charges 
 Once created, 
 these overhead components can be used inside the BOM Overhead Cost section.

title: BOM Register
text:
BOM Register 
 Reports" />
 BOM Register 
 The BOM Register report displays details 
 related to the Bill Of Material (BOM). 
 It shows the structure of finished goods 
 and the raw materials required for production.

title: Jobber Bill of Material
text:
Jobber Bill of Material 
 Help > Setup > General" />
 Jobber Bill 
 of Material 
 The Jobber Bill Of Material is used 
 for Job Work Production. Job work means production is performed by an 
 external vendor or subcontractor instead of inside the company. These 
 vendors are called Jobbers. 
 In 
 this setup, a BOM is created specifically for job work production. Jobbers 
 are selected from the Ledger Master. 
 Conditions 
 Ledger 
 Type must be Supplier 
 Subcontractor 
 option must be enabled 
 Key Features 
 Jobber 
 Wise BOM - Separate BOM can be created for different jobbers. 
 Item 
 Wise Labour Rate - Labour charges can be defined for each jobber and 
 item combination. 
 Example : Jobber A may charge ₹5 per 
 unit and Jobber B may charge ₹7 per unit. 
 All other configurations 
 remain similar to the normal BOM structure.

title: Production
text:
Production 
 Help > Transactions > General" />
 Production 
 The Production Entry is used to record 
 the actual manufacturing activity. In this transaction, the system records 
 the finished goods produced, raw materials consumed, production losses, 
 and overhead costs. 
 Production entries 
 can be created in two ways: 
 With Production Work Order 
 Without Production Work Order 
 This flexibility 
 allows companies to follow either a planned production process or a direct 
 production process. 
 Explore business use cases: Multiple 
 Production Option and Contractor 
 Production . 
 Main Info 
 In 
 this section, users enter basic production details. 
 Produced Item Info 
 The finished goods 
 item can be selected manually from the Material Item Master or automatically 
 fetched from the Production Work Order. 
 Item Info 
 Warehouse - The warehouse where the finished goods 
 will be stored is selected from the Warehouse Master available in 
 the Material Module. 
 Production Quantity - The quantity of finished 
 goods to be produced can either: 
 Come automatically from the work 
 order 
 Be entered manually by the user 
 BOM 
 Variant - Users can select the required BOM variant defined in the 
 Bill Of Material setup. If no BOM is selected, the production can 
 still be recorded manually. 
 Machine Information 
 - The machine used for production can be selected from the Item Master 
 where capitalization-based items are maintained. This information 
 is mainly used for reporting and machine performance analysis. 
 Finished 
 Goods Value - The system calculates the value of finished goods based 
 on the following components: Finished Goods Value = Raw Material Consumed 
 Value + Overhead Cost 
 Posting Info 
 Accounting impact 
 Finished goods stock account will be debited 
 Goods consumed account will be credited 
 The exact accounting 
 entry depends on the item type configuration. 
 Abnormal 
 Loss or Gain (Item Info) 
 During 
 production, sometimes the actual material consumption may differ from 
 the expected quantity. 
 The system calculates 
 abnormal loss or gain based on the following formula: 
 Actual 
 Consumption Quantity = Consumption Quantity + Normal Loss + Abnormal Loss 
 or Gain 
 Abnormal Loss 
 or Gain = Total Quantity – Actual Quantity 
 If abnormal 
 loss or gain occurs, selecting an abnormal loss reason from the setup 
 becomes mandatory. 
 Accounting Impact 
 of Raw Material Consumption 
 When 
 raw materials are consumed during production: 
 The 
 raw material stock account will be credited 
 The 
 Goods Consumed General Ledger account will be debited 
 This ensures 
 proper inventory and accounting tracking. 
 Overhead Cost Info 
 This section 
 records indirect production costs. Overhead costs can be added in two 
 ways. 
 BOM Based Overhead Cost - If overhead components 
 are defined in the BOM, the system automatically fetches them. 
 Manual Overhead Cost - If no overhead components 
 are defined in the BOM, users can manually enter overhead costs. 
 Accounting Impact 
 of Overhead Cost 
 The system performs the following accounting entries: 
 Overhead cost will be credited to 
 the system generated overhead cost account 
 Goods consumed account will be debited 
 Overhead components must be created 
 in the Production Overhead Cost setup, which was explained earlier. 
 Breakdown Info 
 This section 
 is used to record machine breakdown information during production. 
 Users can enter: 
 Breakdown reason and Breakdown duration 
 The 
 breakdown reasons are selected from the Break Down Master setup. 
 Accounting 
 impact 
 Finished 
 goods stock account will be debited 
 Goods 
 consumed account will be credited 
 The 
 exact accounting entry depends on the item type configuration. 
 Multiple 
 Production Option 
 Produced Item Information - In the multiple production 
 mode, this section is used to define the produced items. 
 Users can enter: 
 Multiple finished goods items 
 Line wise BOM selection 
 Warehouse details 
 Production quantity 
 Contractor 
 Production in Production Entry 
 After receiving raw materials, the contractor performs 
 the required production work. Once the production is completed, the production 
 activity needs to be recorded in the system. This transaction is known 
 as Contractor Production. In this process, the system records: 
 • Finished 
 goods produced by the contractor 
 • Raw 
 materials consumed during job work production 
 • Contractor 
 information related to the production activity 
 • Main Information: 
 Document 
 Type - While creating the contractor production 
 entry, the user must select the document type: Jobber Production (JPROD). 
 Selecting this document type enables contractor related fields in 
 the transaction. 
 Produced Item - The finished goods item produced 
 by the contractor must be selected. 
 Item 
 Information - The Item Information section works in the same way as 
 normal production. 
 Here users 
 can define: Raw materials consumed during production, Quantity 
 of materials used and Loss or gain if applicable.

title: Prime Cost Variance Analysis
text:
Prime Cost Variance Analysis 
 Reports" />
 Prime 
 Cost Variance Analysis 
 Prime 
 Cost Variance Analysis Register Summary 
 • The 
 Prime Cost Variance Analysis Register Summary report provides a summarized 
 view of cost variance related to production. 
 • This 
 report compares the expected production cost with the actual production 
 cost recorded during production transactions. 
 It helps management 
 analyze: 
 o Whether 
 production costs are higher than expected 
 o Whether 
 materials are being consumed more than planned 
 o Cost 
 variations in the manufacturing process 
 Prime Cost Variance Analysis (MIS Report) 
 • A 
 new report called Prime Cost Variance Analysis has been introduced in 
 the Production Module. This is a Management Information System (MIS) report 
 used to analyze the difference between the expected production cost and 
 the actual production cost. 
 • In 
 production, the Bill Of Material defines the expected quantity of raw 
 materials required to produce finished goods. However, during actual production, 
 the quantity of materials consumed may sometimes differ due to: 
 o Production 
 loss 
 o Operational 
 variations 
 o Manual 
 adjustments 
 o Efficiency 
 differences in the production process 
 • This 
 report compares: 
 o Cost 
 calculated based on BOM 
 o Actual 
 cost based on real material consumption
